chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Khalid narrated from Abu Al-Hasan Al-Awwal (peace be upon him) that he was asked about a man who approached another man while he was lying down. When he got on top of him, the man woke up and struck him with a severe blow, killing him.
He said: "There is neither blood money for him nor retaliation."

key_terms.بَعْجَة: A severe, forceful blow or strike
key_terms.دِيَة: Blood money (compensation for death or injury)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on retaliation and blood money if a sleeping man kills his attacker who woke him up?
ai.summary: In this ruling from Imam al-Rida (AS), the killer is exempt from both *qisas* (retaliation) and *diyah* (blood money) because the sleeping man’s strike was a spontaneous, defensive reaction to an unexpected intrusion, lacking the element of premeditated aggression. This highlights the Shia jurisprudential principle that immediate self-defense against a sudden, unprovoked attack by the victim absolves the attacker of full liability, distinguishing it from cases of deliberate homicide. The exemption underscores the fairness of the law in recognizing the natural reflex of a sleeper caught off-guard.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.5360 - Al-Husayn ibn Khalid narrated from Abu Al-Hasan Al-Awwal (as) that he was asked about a man who approached another man while he was lying down. When he got on top of him, the man woke up and struck him with a severe blow, killing him.
Imam (as) said: "There is neither blood money (compensation) for him nor retaliation (legal retribution)."
